summary: The four originally cited SYN-001 paragraphs and detailed footnote now distinguish Augustine's general good-works explanation from the study's practical-mercy application. One equivalent attribution remains in 40-charity-within.tex:35. All five HOM-001 addressee recurrences are corrected, and the complete homily remains intelligible with accurate delivery estimates and source limits.

advisories.rationale: The inspected NPNF Psalm LXIII section 10 links hands lifted in prayer with exercise in good works, after discussing Christ's outstretched hands and mercy through the Cross. It does not specify aid to the needy at that locus. Each corrected paragraph now credits Augustine with good works and marks practical mercy as the application considered here. Bodily resurrection and ordinary sleep remain supported in sections 2, 4-5 and 12. The remaining recurrence is finding ASR-001.

All five direct requests now identify the Lord as addressee and his Spirit as the means of sustaining or preserving integrity. The Latin page images explicitly carry Domine and per infusionem Spiritus tui; the FDLC approved English excerpt distinguishes O Lord from your Spirit. The qualified U.S. 2011 image agrees. Remaining descriptions such as petition for the Spirit's preservation describe the requested work without assigning the prayer to the Spirit as addressee.

findings.problem: His conjunction of raised hands and mercy attributes the practical-mercy conjunction directly to Augustine, immediately after his Psalm 62 exposition and before action toward a neighbor. The checked section 10 states good works generally, with divine mercy through Christ's Cross; it does not make the particular neighbor-directed application as phrased here. This is an additional occurrence of the same attribution precision issue the requested correction is meant to resolve.
findings.required_result: Credit Augustine here with joining raised hands and good works, preserving the following neighbor-directed consequence as the study's application. A local change from mercy to good works in the first sentence will remove the specific false attribution without altering the argument.
